mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within two months signals economic distress, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the unemployment rate increased by more than 0.5% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending rise.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 35% of the instances where housing starts increased for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over two months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth slows and corporate earnings decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where industrial production decreased by more than 2% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% over two months signals a strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where real personal consumption expenditures increased by more than 1% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate was above 2% and the consumer price index increased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same month, it signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as economic optimism rises.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 30% of the instances where nonfarm payrolls increased by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate decreased by more than 0.2% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a robust economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic outlook improve.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 35% of the instances where GDP increased for two consecutive quarters.
